A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FALCON and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures. V1 includes supplementary Appendices A–D; v2 ends after the references. This omission can be compared directly and is not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original FALCON-3B and FALCON-7B benchmark results, component ablations, register-count experiments, and qualitative analyses, including supplementary attention visualizations.

after.justification: V2 reports original results for its revised FALCON configuration, component ablations, and a new comparison using the same training dataset as LLaVA-v1.5.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the three-stage pipeline into four stages: the initial stages are renumbered, a high-resolution refinement stage is inserted, and final instruction tuning trains the LLM instead of using LoRA with a frozen LLM. V2 also replaces the vision and language backbones. The underlying ReCompact and ReAtten operations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands within the existing vision-language domains: ChartQA and SEED-Img are added to the main comparisons, while the new training-data ablation evaluates GQA and MM-Vet. ChartQA and GQA already appeared among v1's training sources, so their new evaluation role does not establish wholly new task coverage. The original evaluation benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds LLaVA-OneVision and removes Cambrian-1-8B. Figure 4 adds Pixel Shuffle, and the new matched-data experiment compares against LLaVA-v1.5. Monkey also gains a POPE comparison entry. Most existing comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The main configuration changes from CLIP-ViT-L/14 at 336 pixels with Vicuna-7B or Llama-3.2-3B to SigLIP-L/16 at 384 pixels with Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. V2 uses one 64-register configuration and introduces a two-stage, LLaVA-data-matched evaluation. Missing descriptions of retained ablation settings establish documentation loss, not that those experiments were rerun differently.

E4.justification: New Table 3 tests whether FALCON's advantage persists when trained using LLaVA-v1.5's dataset and a two-stage pipeline, adding an important control for training-data differences. The compression ablation adds Pixel Shuffle. The existing ReAtten comparison and register-count analysis remain, but Appendix C and Figure 9's additional attention-map analyses are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. Benchmark averages and the POPE Random split are not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Headline results are extensively replaced: Table 1 reports perception/reasoning Avg scores of 45.9/34.8 for v1's FALCON-7B versus 50.3/40.7 for v2's differently configured FALCON. These are not same-setting gains. V1's 3B results disappear; ChartQA, SEED-Img, and matched-data results are added. Monkey's TextVQA score changes from 64.3 to 65.8. Existing ReAtten and register-count results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The register definitions, concatenation operations, and self-attention, ReAtten, and feedforward formulations in Equations 1–3 are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions—compact register representations and cross-image continuity through ReAtten—remain. The abstract and contribution list narrow the headline compression claim from 9-fold and 16-fold to 9-fold. The adaptation-data claim also changes from fewer than 2M samples to fewer than 3M.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new matched-data comparison as excluding training-data influence and extends the explanation about inadequate redundancy removal to Pixel Shuffle. It removes Appendix D's discussion of inherited hallucination and bias risks and their mitigation. Most interpretations of attention maps, visual continuity, and register-count tradeoffs remain.

D1.justification: Removing Appendices A–B eliminates detailed training-data composition, batch sizes, learning rates, epochs, optimizer settings, hardware, training times, and comparator implementation controls. V2 states its replacement backbones and basic architecture in Section 4 but supplies no equivalent training recipe. The printed repository link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 expands its application discussion to online video assistants, robotic manipulation, and GUI agents, with corresponding new citations. References supporting new comparisons, including InternVL and LLaVA-OneVision, are added; several dataset and LoRA references disappear with the supplement. The central positioning against compression modules and fragmented cropping remains.

P1.justification: The main section order and much of the prose remain. V2 moves and revises the Abstractor comparison into the introduction, expands the applications paragraph, rewrites the training subsection, and adjusts experimental narration. It also adds Miao Zhang to the author list and removes the supplementary sections.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn for four training stages, Figure 4 gains Pixel Shuffle bars, and Table 1 is regrouped by visual-token budget instead of training-corpus size. V2 adds a training-data ablation table and ChartQA/SEED-Img columns. The supplementary dataset table and Figure 9 disappear; most other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The matched-data comparison, Pixel Shuffle baseline, and additional evaluations provide useful evidence. However, v2 removes the detailed training recipes and ablation controls precisely while changing the backbones and training pipeline, and also drops the limitations discussion. The resulting loss of reproducibility and transparency outweighs the added validation; higher scores under changed settings do not establish a controlled improvement.
